[4] The i.MX 93 Applications Processor is a new CPU generation with many advantages High flexibility based on the latest technologies WHITEPAPER  WHITEPAPER | The i.MX 93 Applications Processor is a new CPU generation with many advantages 2 How does the i.MX 93 processor fit into the i.MX 9 series? 3 Module Designs i.MX 93 processor 5 Mainboard Design 7 Available modules/mainboards of the i.MX 93 processor from TQ 15 Additional Information 18 Content  WHITEPAPER | The i.MX 93 Applications Processor is a new CPU generation with many advantages 3 The i.MX 93 processor How does the i.MX 93 processor fit into the i.MX 9 series? The i.MX 93 processor uses the Cortex A55 core with clock speeds up to 1.7 GHz. The Cortex-A55 processor core uses DynamIQ technology (the successor to Arm‘s big.LITTLE concept) and features the latest enhancements to the ARMv8.2-A architecture with a dedicated instruc­ tion set to accelerate machine learning (ML) models. According to NXP, the i.MX 93 processor is the first in the industry to implement ARM‘s Ethos-U65 microNPU with a performance of 256 MACs/cycle. The Ethos-U65 offers a very good combination of performance and efficiency in a very small size, enabling developers to realize high- performance, low-cost and energy-efficient ML applications. The i.MX 93 processor also contains a 250 MHz Cortex-M33 processor core for time-critical real-time computation and control and the EdgeLock Secure Enclave for providing the security functions. The memory interface is 16-bit wide and supports LPDDR4 and LPDDR4X with internal ECC support. In addition to up to 7 x I²S audio interfaces and 8-channel PDM microphone inputs, the processor offers extensive interfaces: CAN-FD, UARTs, SPI, QSPI, I²C and SDIO. Extensive security functions are also implemented. With the i.MX 93 processor, NXP offers a price- and feature-optimized CPU from the i.MX 9 series. Next to the i.MX 91 processor, the i.MX 93 processor is the smallest CPU in the i.MX 9 series and a good alternative to the i.MX 28 processor, i.MX 6UL/i.MX 6ULL processor for new designs. The main difference between this CPU and its pre­ decessors in terms of graphics and video interfaces is the addition of 24-bit RGB, MIPI-DSI and LVDS interfaces. A total of four CPU variants are available, from single-core to dual-core with/without NPU and qualified to operate at different temperature range The most important interfaces are available as follows: • 1x MIPI DSI 4 Lanes (display serial interface) • 1x LVDS 4 Lanes • 1x MIPI CSI 2 Lanes (camera sensor interface) • 3x SDIO supporting SD/eMMC/Wi-Fi • 2x USB 2.0 • 2x Gigabit Ethernet (1x TSN) • 2x CAN-FD • 8x UART, 8x I²C, 8x SPI, 7x I²S • 1x QSPI • 1x 4-ch, 12-bit ADC A serial camera interface (MIPI-CSI) allows a camera to be connected directly to the CPU and supports its use in digital imaging applications. The i.MX 93 processor is based on the same Arm Core architecture as the entire i.MX 9 series.

[3] The i.MX 93 Applications Processor is a new CPU generation with many advantages High flexibility based on the latest technologies WHITEPAPER  WHITEPAPER | The i.MX 93 Applications Processor is a new CPU generation with many advantages 2 How does the i.MX 93 processor fit into the i.MX 9 series? 3 Module Designs i.MX 93 processor 5 Mainboard Design 7 Available modules/mainboards of the i.MX 93 processor from TQ 15 Additional Information 18 Content  WHITEPAPER | The i.MX 93 Applications Processor is a new CPU generation with many advantages 3 The i.MX 93 processor How does the i.MX 93 processor fit into the i.MX 9 series? The i.MX 93 processor uses the Cortex A55 core with clock speeds up to 1.7 GHz. The Cortex-A55 processor core uses DynamIQ technology (the successor to Arm‘s big.LITTLE concept) and features the latest enhancements to the ARMv8.2-A architecture with a dedicated instruc­ tion set to accelerate machine learning (ML) models. According to NXP, the i.MX 93 processor is the first in the industry to implement ARM‘s Ethos-U65 microNPU with a performance of 256 MACs/cycle. The Ethos-U65 offers a very good combination of performance and efficiency in a very small size, enabling developers to realize high- performance, low-cost and energy-efficient ML applications. The i.MX 93 processor also contains a 250 MHz Cortex-M33 processor core for time-critical real-time computation and control and the EdgeLock Secure Enclave for providing the security functions. The memory interface is 16-bit wide and supports LPDDR4 and LPDDR4X with internal ECC support. In addition to up to 7 x I²S audio interfaces and 8-channel PDM microphone inputs, the processor offers extensive interfaces: CAN-FD, UARTs, SPI, QSPI, I²C and SDIO. Extensive security functions are also implemented. With the i.MX 93 processor, NXP offers a price- and feature-optimized CPU from the i.MX 9 series. Next to the i.MX 91 processor, the i.MX 93 processor is the smallest CPU in the i.MX 9 series and a good alternative to the i.MX 28 processor, i.MX 6UL/i.MX 6ULL processor for new designs. The main difference between this CPU and its pre­ decessors in terms of graphics and video interfaces is the addition of 24-bit RGB, MIPI-DSI and LVDS interfaces. A total of four CPU variants are available, from single-core to dual-core with/without NPU and qualified to operate at different temperature range The most important interfaces are available as follows: • 1x MIPI DSI 4 Lanes (display serial interface) • 1x LVDS 4 Lanes • 1x MIPI CSI 2 Lanes (camera sensor interface) • 3x SDIO supporting SD/eMMC/Wi-Fi • 2x USB 2.0 • 2x Gigabit Ethernet (1x TSN) • 2x CAN-FD • 8x UART, 8x I²C, 8x SPI, 7x I²S • 1x QSPI • 1x 4-ch, 12-bit ADC A serial camera interface (MIPI-CSI) allows a camera to be connected directly to the CPU and supports its use in digital imaging applications. The i.MX 93 processor is based on the same Arm Core architecture as the entire i.MX 9 series.

The i.MX 93 processor uses the Cortex A55 core with clock speeds up to 1.7 GHz. The Cortex-A55 processor core uses DynamIQ technology (the successor to Arm‘s big.LITTLE concept) and features the latest enhancements to the ARMv8.2-A architecture with a dedicated instruc­ tion set to accelerate machine learning (ML) models. According to NXP, the i.MX 93 processor is the first in the industry to implement ARM‘s Ethos-U65 microNPU with a performance of 256 MACs/cycle. The Ethos-U65 offers a very good combination of performance and efficiency in a very small size, enabling developers to realize high- performance, low-cost and energy-efficient ML applications. The i.MX 93 processor also contains a 250 MHz Cortex-M33 processor core for time-critical real-time computation and control and the EdgeLock Secure Enclave for providing the security functions. The memory interface is 16-bit wide and supports LPDDR4 and LPDDR4X with internal ECC support. In addition to up to 7 x I²S audio interfaces and 8-channel PDM microphone inputs, the processor offers extensive interfaces: CAN-FD, UARTs, SPI, QSPI, I²C and SDIO. Extensive security functions are also implemented. With the i.MX 93 processor, NXP offers a price- and feature-optimized CPU from the i.MX 9 series. Next to the i.MX 91 processor, the i.MX 93 processor is the smallest CPU in the i.MX 9 series and a good alternative to the i.MX 28 processor, i.MX 6UL/i.MX 6ULL processor for new designs. The main difference between this CPU and its pre­ decessors in terms of graphics and video interfaces is the addition of 24-bit RGB, MIPI-DSI and LVDS interfaces. A total of four CPU variants are available, from single-core to dual-core with/without NPU and qualified to operate at different temperature range The most important interfaces are available as follows: • 1x MIPI DSI 4 Lanes (display serial interface) • 1x LVDS 4 Lanes • 1x MIPI CSI 2 Lanes (camera sensor interface) • 3x SDIO supporting SD/eMMC/Wi-Fi • 2x USB 2.0 • 2x Gigabit Ethernet (1x TSN) • 2x CAN-FD • 8x UART, 8x I²C, 8x SPI, 7x I²S • 1x QSPI • 1x 4-ch, 12-bit ADC A serial camera interface (MIPI-CSI) allows a camera to be connected directly to the CPU and supports its use in digital imaging applications. The i.MX 93 processor is based on the same Arm Core architecture as the entire i.MX 9 series.

The i.MX 93 processor uses the Cortex A55 core with clock speeds up to 1.7 GHz. The Cortex-A55 processor core uses DynamIQ technology (the successor to Arm‘s big.LITTLE concept) and features the latest enhancements to the ARMv8.2-A architecture with a dedicated instruc­ tion set to accelerate machine learning (ML) models. According to NXP, the i.MX 93 processor is the first in the industry to implement ARM‘s Ethos-U65 microNPU with a performance of 256 MACs/cycle. The Ethos-U65 offers a very good combination of performance and efficiency in a very small size, enabling developers to realize high- performance, low-cost and energy-efficient ML applications. The i.MX 93 processor also contains a 250 MHz Cortex-M33 processor core for time-critical real-time computation and control and the EdgeLock Secure Enclave for providing the security functions. The memory interface is 16-bit wide and supports LPDDR4 and LPDDR4X with internal ECC support. In addition to up to 7 x I²S audio interfaces and 8-channel PDM microphone inputs, the processor offers extensive interfaces: CAN-FD, UARTs, SPI, QSPI, I²C and SDIO. Extensive security functions are also implemented. With the i.MX 93 processor, NXP offers a price- and feature-optimized CPU from the i.MX 9 series. Next to the i.MX 91 processor, the i.MX 93 processor is the smallest CPU in the i.MX 9 series and a good alternative to the i.MX 28 processor, i.MX 6UL/i.MX 6ULL processor for new designs. The main difference between this CPU and its pre­ decessors in terms of graphics and video interfaces is the addition of 24-bit RGB, MIPI-DSI and LVDS interfaces. A total of four CPU variants are available, from single-core to dual-core with/without NPU and qualified to operate at different temperature range The most important interfaces are available as follows: • 1x MIPI DSI 4 Lanes (display serial interface) • 1x LVDS 4 Lanes • 1x MIPI CSI 2 Lanes (camera sensor interface) • 3x SDIO supporting SD/eMMC/Wi-Fi • 2x USB 2.0 • 2x Gigabit Ethernet (1x TSN) • 2x CAN-FD • 8x UART, 8x I²C, 8x SPI, 7x I²S • 1x QSPI • 1x 4-ch, 12-bit ADC A serial camera interface (MIPI-CSI) allows a camera to be connected directly to the CPU and supports its use in digital imaging applications. The i.MX 93 processor is based on the same Arm Core architecture as the entire i.MX 9 series.

rows.raw:
The i.MX 93 and i.MX 95 differ in their Arm Cortex-A core configurations:

- **i.MX 93**: It uses the Arm Cortex-A55 core. Specifically, it has 6x Arm Cortex-A55 cores, each capable of up to 1.8 GHz frequency.

- **i.MX 95**: It also uses the Arm Cortex-A55 core but has a different core count. The i.MX 95 has up to 6x Arm Cortex-A55 cores as well, with a similar frequency range.

So, both processors have the same number of Arm Cortex-A55 cores, which is 6 cores each. The key differences between them are in their additional features, such as the Neural Processing Unit (NPU) and other peripherals, rather than the core count.

The sum of the I2C and LPUART instances is:

8 (I2C instances) + 8 (LPUART instances) = 16 instances in total.

rows.raw:
The i.MX 93 includes two LPI2C instances and eight LPUART instances. Here’s the breakdown:

- **LPI2C Instances**: The i.MX 93 includes two LPI2C (Low Power Inter-Integrated Circuit) instances.
- **LPUART Instances**: It includes eight LPUART (Low Power Universal Asynchronous Receiver/Transmitter) instances.

The sum of the two is:
\[ 2 \text{ (LPI2C instances)} + 8 \text{ (LPUART instances)} = 10 \]

So, the total sum of the I2C and LPUART instances is **10**.

rows.raw:
The i.MX 93 applications processor includes the following compute resources:

- **Cortex-A55 Cores**: There are two Cortex-A55 cores. Each core has its own L1 instruction cache (32 KB), L1 data cache (32 KB), and a 64 KB per-core L2 cache. They are also equipped with a Media Processing Engine (MPE) supporting ARM Neon technology, a Floating Point Unit (FPU) with VFPv4-D16 architecture, and a 256 KB cluster L3 cache.

- **Cortex-M33 Core**: There is one Cortex-M33 core. This core supports FPU, MPU, NVIC, FPB, DWT, and ITM. It has a two-way set-associative 16 KB System Cache with parity support and a two-way set-associative 16 KB Code Cache with parity support, along with 256 KB of tightly coupled memory (TCM).

- **Neural Processing Unit (NPU)**: The i.MX 93 includes a Neural Processing Unit (NPU) that provides neural network performance, capable of 256 MACs operating up to 1.0 GHz and 2 OPS/MAC. This NPU is designed to handle 8-bit and 16-bit integer RNN, targeting 8-bit weights.

In summary, the i.MX 93 has two Cortex-A55 cores, one Cortex-M33 core, and one Neural Processing Unit (NPU).

See Arm Cortex-A55 documentation for more information. 12.2.4 Atomic Instructions The Arm Cortex-A55 Core Technical Reference Manual mentions that atomics are supported to cacheable memory but requires a coherent interconnect to support atomics to device or non-cacheable memory. This product does not support such a coherent interconnect. If such an atomic instruction is executed when the interconnect does not support them, it will result in a synchronous Data Abort (for load atomics) or an asynchronous Data Abort (for store atomics) 12.2.5 Debug The Cortex-A55 platform includes the debug and trace sub-modules. The debug interface is connected to the DAP and CoreSight debug modules in the SoC to allow debug through JTAG interface. [1] FACT SHEET i.MX 93 APPLICATIONS PROCESSOR FAMILY i.MX 93 applications processors deliver efficient machine learning (ML) acceleration, energy flex architecture and state-of-the-art security to support energy-efficient edge computing. i.MX 93 processors offer fast and efficient ML inferencing along with a rich set of peripherals and high-performance application cores for automotive, industrial and consumer IoT market segments. TARGET APPLICATIONS • Automotive: domain controller compute off-load engine, driver monitoring system, audio, speech recognition, cost-effective gateway • Industrial Automation: gateways, remote I/O controllers, industrial scanners, HMI, machine vision • Building Control and Energy: energy meters, EV charging • Smart Home: home security hub, smart doorbell, smart lock, smart thermostat, AV receivers • Smart City: smart lighting, safety and security, traffic control PERFORMANCE COMPUTE ENGINE The i.MX 93 applications processors are the first in the i.MX portfolio to integrate the scalable Arm® Cortex®-A55 core, bringing best-in-class performance and energy efficiency to Linux-based edge applications. Based on Arm’s DynamIQ technology, the A55 core features the latest Armv8-A architecture extensions with dedicated instructions to accelerate machine learning (ML). NEURAL PROCESSING UNIT (NPU) The i.MX 93 family marks the industry’s first implementation of the Arm® Ethos™-U65 microNPU. A dedicated neural processing unit (NPU), Ethos-U65 delivers a combination of performance and efficiency with an optimized footprint that enables developers to create high-performance, cost- effective and energy-efficient ML applications. BUILT-IN MCU A 250 MHz Arm® Cortex®-M33 processor performs time- critical real-time compute and control. It can eliminate the need for an external microcontroller in the system design. The integrated Cortex-M33 core associated with the CAN FD interfaces provides a robust local control network for industrial applications. Additionally, the built-in Arm Cortex M33 in conjunction with the NPU can be used for low-power wake-word detection. i.MX 93 APPLICATIONS PROCESSOR FAMILY  [url] 2 CAMERA INTERFACES AND IMAGE PROCESSING The i.MX 93 family contains MIPI-CSI and parallel image sensor interfaces along with the NPU to support both monochrome and RGB (color) vision applications. The application processor offers a 2-lane MIPI-CSI camera interface capable of supporting 1080-p60 resolution and enables direct connection to external camera module and ISP. The application processors offer capabilities including down scaling, color space conversion, de-interlacing, alpha insertion, cropping and rotation of images for machine vision and other ML-related applications. DISPLAY AND MULTIMEDIA The i.MX 93 applications processors contain a 4-lane MIPI-DSI capable of supporting 1080p60 resolution, a 4-lane LVDS and parallel display interfaces capable of 720p60 resolution. Additionally, it features a high-efficiency pixel pipeline to perform 2D graphics processing to realize cost-effective GUI solutions. It is capable of image rotation (90°, 180°, 270°), image resize, color space conversion, multiple pixel format support (RGB, YUV444, YUV422, YUV420, YUV400) and standard 2D-DMA operations. SYSTEM SECURITY The i.MX 93 family implements security via NXP’s EdgeLock® secure enclave, a preconfigured, self-managed and autonomous security subsystem.

The i.MX 93 processor uses the Cortex A55 core with clock speeds up to 1.7 GHz. The Cortex-A55 processor core uses DynamIQ technology (the successor to Arm‘s big.LITTLE concept) and features the latest enhancements to the ARMv8.2-A architecture with a dedicated instruc­ tion set to accelerate machine learning (ML) models. According to NXP, the i.MX 93 processor is the first in the industry to implement ARM‘s Ethos-U65 microNPU with a performance of 256 MACs/cycle. The Ethos-U65 offers a very good combination of performance and efficiency in a very small size, enabling developers to realize high- performance, low-cost and energy-efficient ML applications. The i.MX 93 processor also contains a 250 MHz Cortex-M33 processor core for time-critical real-time computation and control and the EdgeLock Secure Enclave for providing the security functions. The memory interface is 16-bit wide and supports LPDDR4 and LPDDR4X with internal ECC support. In addition to up to 7 x I²S audio interfaces and 8-channel PDM microphone inputs, the processor offers extensive interfaces: CAN-FD, UARTs, SPI, QSPI, I²C and SDIO. Extensive security functions are also implemented. With the i.MX 93 processor, NXP offers a price- and feature-optimized CPU from the i.MX 9 series. Next to the i.MX 91 processor, the i.MX 93 processor is the smallest CPU in the i.MX 9 series and a good alternative to the i.MX 28 processor, i.MX 6UL/i.MX 6ULL processor for new designs. The main difference between this CPU and its pre­ decessors in terms of graphics and video interfaces is the addition of 24-bit RGB, MIPI-DSI and LVDS interfaces. A total of four CPU variants are available, from single-core to dual-core with/without NPU and qualified to operate at different temperature range The most important interfaces are available as follows: • 1x MIPI DSI 4 Lanes (display serial interface) • 1x LVDS 4 Lanes • 1x MIPI CSI 2 Lanes (camera sensor interface) • 3x SDIO supporting SD/eMMC/Wi-Fi • 2x USB 2.0 • 2x Gigabit Ethernet (1x TSN) • 2x CAN-FD • 8x UART, 8x I²C, 8x SPI, 7x I²S • 1x QSPI • 1x 4-ch, 12-bit ADC A serial camera interface (MIPI-CSI) allows a camera to be connected directly to the CPU and supports its use in digital imaging applications. The i.MX 93 processor is based on the same Arm Core architecture as the entire i.MX 9 series.

TARGET APPLICATIONS • Automotive: domain controller compute off-load engine, driver monitoring system, audio, speech recognition, cost-effective gateway • Industrial Automation: gateways, remote I/O controllers, industrial scanners, HMI, machine vision • Building Control and Energy: energy meters, EV charging • Smart Home: home security hub, smart doorbell, smart lock, smart thermostat, AV receivers • Smart City: smart lighting, safety and security, traffic control PERFORMANCE COMPUTE ENGINE The i.MX 93 applications processors are the first in the i.MX portfolio to integrate the scalable Arm® Cortex®-A55 core, bringing best-in-class performance and energy efficiency to Linux-based edge applications. Based on Arm’s DynamIQ technology, the A55 core features the latest Armv8-A architecture extensions with dedicated instructions to accelerate machine learning (ML). NEURAL PROCESSING UNIT (NPU) The i.MX 93 family marks the industry’s first implementation of the Arm® Ethos™-U65 microNPU. A dedicated neural processing unit (NPU), Ethos-U65 delivers a combination of performance and efficiency with an optimized footprint that enables developers to create high-performance, cost- effective and energy-efficient ML applications. BUILT-IN MCU A 250 MHz Arm® Cortex®-M33 processor performs time- critical real-time compute and control. It can eliminate the need for an external microcontroller in the system design. The integrated Cortex-M33 core associated with the CAN FD interfaces provides a robust local control network for industrial applications. Additionally, the built-in Arm Cortex M33 in conjunction with the NPU can be used for low-power wake-word detection. i.MX 93 APPLICATIONS PROCESSOR FAMILY  [url] 2 CAMERA INTERFACES AND IMAGE PROCESSING The i.MX 93 family contains MIPI-CSI and parallel image sensor interfaces along with the NPU to support both monochrome and RGB (color) vision applications. The application processor offers a 2-lane MIPI-CSI camera interface capable of supporting 1080-p60 resolution and enables direct connection to external camera module and ISP. The application processors offer capabilities including down scaling, color space conversion, de-interlacing, alpha insertion, cropping and rotation of images for machine vision and other ML-related applications. DISPLAY AND MULTIMEDIA The i.MX 93 applications processors contain a 4-lane MIPI-DSI capable of supporting 1080p60 resolution, a 4-lane LVDS and parallel display interfaces capable of 720p60 resolution. Additionally, it features a high-efficiency pixel pipeline to perform 2D graphics processing to realize cost-effective GUI solutions. It is capable of image rotation (90°, 180°, 270°), image resize, color space conversion, multiple pixel format support (RGB, YUV444, YUV422, YUV420, YUV400) and standard 2D-DMA operations. SYSTEM SECURITY The i.MX 93 family implements security via NXP’s EdgeLock® secure enclave, a preconfigured, self-managed and autonomous security subsystem.

[3] The i.MX 93 Applications Processor is a new CPU generation with many advantages High flexibility based on the latest technologies WHITEPAPER  WHITEPAPER | The i.MX 93 Applications Processor is a new CPU generation with many advantages 2 How does the i.MX 93 processor fit into the i.MX 9 series? 3 Module Designs i.MX 93 processor 5 Mainboard Design 7 Available modules/mainboards of the i.MX 93 processor from TQ 15 Additional Information 18 Content  WHITEPAPER | The i.MX 93 Applications Processor is a new CPU generation with many advantages 3 The i.MX 93 processor How does the i.MX 93 processor fit into the i.MX 9 series? The i.MX 93 processor uses the Cortex A55 core with clock speeds up to 1.7 GHz. The Cortex-A55 processor core uses DynamIQ technology (the successor to Arm‘s big.LITTLE concept) and features the latest enhancements to the ARMv8.2-A architecture with a dedicated instruc­ tion set to accelerate machine learning (ML) models. According to NXP, the i.MX 93 processor is the first in the industry to implement ARM‘s Ethos-U65 microNPU with a performance of 256 MACs/cycle. The Ethos-U65 offers a very good combination of performance and efficiency in a very small size, enabling developers to realize high- performance, low-cost and energy-efficient ML applications. The i.MX 93 processor also contains a 250 MHz Cortex-M33 processor core for time-critical real-time computation and control and the EdgeLock Secure Enclave for providing the security functions. The memory interface is 16-bit wide and supports LPDDR4 and LPDDR4X with internal ECC support. In addition to up to 7 x I²S audio interfaces and 8-channel PDM microphone inputs, the processor offers extensive interfaces: CAN-FD, UARTs, SPI, QSPI, I²C and SDIO. Extensive security functions are also implemented. With the i.MX 93 processor, NXP offers a price- and feature-optimized CPU from the i.MX 9 series. Next to the i.MX 91 processor, the i.MX 93 processor is the smallest CPU in the i.MX 9 series and a good alternative to the i.MX 28 processor, i.MX 6UL/i.MX 6ULL processor for new designs. The main difference between this CPU and its pre­ decessors in terms of graphics and video interfaces is the addition of 24-bit RGB, MIPI-DSI and LVDS interfaces. A total of four CPU variants are available, from single-core to dual-core with/without NPU and qualified to operate at different temperature range The most important interfaces are available as follows: • 1x MIPI DSI 4 Lanes (display serial interface) • 1x LVDS 4 Lanes • 1x MIPI CSI 2 Lanes (camera sensor interface) • 3x SDIO supporting SD/eMMC/Wi-Fi • 2x USB 2.0 • 2x Gigabit Ethernet (1x TSN) • 2x CAN-FD • 8x UART, 8x I²C, 8x SPI, 7x I²S • 1x QSPI • 1x 4-ch, 12-bit ADC A serial camera interface (MIPI-CSI) allows a camera to be connected directly to the CPU and supports its use in digital imaging applications. The i.MX 93 processor is based on the same Arm Core architecture as the entire i.MX 9 series.

Subject: Introducing the NXP i.MX 95: Perfect for Our Next Edge-AI Product

Hi [Colleague's Name],

I hope this email finds you well. I wanted to share some exciting news about the NXP i.MX 95, which I believe will be a fantastic fit for our new edge-AI product. Let me give you a quick rundown on what it is, its Neutron NPU, and why it suits edge inference.

### Overview of the NXP i.MX 95
The NXP i.MX 95 is a powerful applications processor designed for energy-efficient edge computing. It features up to six Arm Cortex-A55 cores, delivering efficient CPU performance for a wide range of applications. The i.MX 95 is also the first i.MX device to support functional safety, integrating an Arm Cortex-M33 platform for safety-critical tasks. Additionally, it includes an extensive set of peripherals tailored for automotive, industrial, and commercial IoT markets.

### Neutron NPU: Enhancing Machine Learning Capabilities
One of the standout features of the i.MX 95 is the Neutron NPU, a hardware accelerator that provides efficient processing of machine-learning workloads. The Neutron NPU is designed to work in conjunction with the CPU to deliver higher performance and lower power consumption for neural network (NN) inference. Here are some key points from the datasheet:

- **Block Diagram**: The Neutron NPU architecture includes components like the Activation Engine, Buffers, Bus Interfaces, and Control, each optimized for specific tasks in the machine learning pipeline.
- **Performance**: The NPU can handle Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) computations efficiently, making it ideal for running complex machine learning models at the edge.
- **Features**: The Neutron NPU supports various operators, including rescaling, activation, and pooling functions, which are essential for neural network inference. It also manages memory accesses and optimizes the arrangement of weights, enhancing overall performance.

### Why the i.MX 95 Suits Edge Inference
The i.MX 95’s combination of powerful CPU cores and the Neutron NPU makes it an excellent choice for edge inference tasks. Here’s why:

- **Efficiency**: The CPU cores provide the necessary compute power, while the NPU optimizes and accelerates the machine learning tasks, ensuring efficient use of resources.
- **Power Efficiency**: The Neutron NPU’s design is optimized for low power consumption, which is crucial for edge devices where power is a limiting factor.
- **Scalability**: With the Neutron NPU, we can deploy machine learning models on the edge without compromising performance, making it suitable for a wide range of applications from autonomous driving to industrial IoT.

I’ve attached the relevant sections from the i.MX 95 Data Sheet for your reference. I’d be happy to discuss this further and explore

claims: Subject: Introducing the NXP i.MX 95 for Our Next-Gen Edge-AI Product
I hope this email finds you well.
I wanted to share some exciting news about the NXP i.MX 95, which we can consider for our upcoming edge-AI product.
The i.MX 95 is a powerful and flexible platform that's perfect for our needs, especially when it comes to edge inference.
The i.MX 95 is an advanced applications processor from NXP, featuring a rich set of peripherals and processor cores tailored for a variety of use cases, including edge computing.
It integrates up to six Arm Cortex-A55 cores, which provide efficient CPU performance, and an innovative Energy Flex architecture that optimizes performance and power efficiency.
The i.MX 95 also supports functional safety, making it suitable for critical applications.
A key feature of the i.MX 95 is the Neutron NPU, which stands out for its efficient processing of machine-learning workloads.
Architecture**: The Neutron N3-1024S NPU is designed to handle Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) operations efficiently, crucial for neural network inference.
Memory**: It has 1492 kB of OCRAM (On-Chip RAM) that can be used for efficient data buffering and processing.
Features**: The NPU supports various operations such as activation functions, rescaling, and pooling, which are essential for neural network inference.
It also includes a weight decoder and rescaler/shifter to optimize the processing of weights and results.
Efficient Performance**: The Neutron NPU is optimized for MAC operations, making it highly efficient for edge inference tasks.
This means we can achieve good inference performance without excessive power consumption.
Flexibility**: The i.MX 95's combination of CPU cores and Neutron NPU allows us to handle a wide range of tasks, from complex AI inference to general-purpose computing.
Scalability**: With the ability to deploy the same neural net across different NXP processors, we can offer a range of products catering to different performance and cost requirements.
For example, we can use the i.MX8 Quad Max for high-performance edge computing and the i.MXRT for lower-cost, lower-power inference.
CPU**: 6x Arm Cortex-A55, up to 1.8 GHz frequency, with 512 kB L3 cache (shared across all cores, ECC protected).
Memory Interface**: Supports up to 19 x 19 mm package with one x32 LPDDR

Subject: Introducing NXP i.MX 95 for Our Next-Gen Edge-AI Product

Hi [Colleague's Name],

I hope this email finds you well. I wanted to share some exciting news about the NXP i.MX 95, which I believe will be a perfect fit for our new edge-AI product. Let me give you a quick rundown on what it is, its Neutron NPU, and why it’s ideal for edge inference.

### NXP i.MX 95 Overview

The NXP i.MX 95 is a powerful applications processor designed for advanced graphics, video, and machine learning acceleration. It features a rich set of peripherals and processor cores that support these features, making it an excellent choice for energy-efficient edge computing. Here are some key details:

- **Processor Cores**: 
  - 6x Arm Cortex-A55 cores, up to 1.8 GHz.
  - 1x Arm Cortex-M7 for real-time processing.
  - 1x Arm Cortex-M33 for safety-critical tasks.

- **Memory**: 
  - Supports up to 6400 MT/s in LPDDR5 mode.
  - High-speed interfaces like MIPI DSI, LVDS, and SPI.

- **Security**: 
  - Integrated EdgeLock secure enclave for enhanced security.

- **Neutron NPU**: 
  - The NPU (Neuron Processing Unit) is a hardware accelerator that provides efficient processing of machine-learning workloads.
  - It supports up to 256 MACs/cycle, making it highly efficient for inference tasks.
  - Features like Weight Decoder, Rescaler/Shifter, and Activation Engine enable optimized neural network processing.

### Why the i.MX 95 Suits Edge Inference

1. **Efficiency**: The Neutron NPU is designed to handle the computational demands of neural networks efficiently, reducing the burden on the main CPU. This not only improves performance but also conserves power, which is crucial for edge devices.
   
2. **Customization**: The NPU supports a wide range of machine learning models, and its architecture allows for efficient memory management and data flow, which is essential for edge inference.

3. **Scalability**: The i.MX 95 supports both low-power and high-performance inference, depending on the requirements of your application. Whether you need fast inference times or lower power consumption, the i.MX 95 can handle it.

4. **Security**: The integrated EdgeLock secure enclave ensures that sensitive data remains secure, which is a critical consideration for edge devices.

In summary, the NXP i.MX 95 with its Neutron NPU is a versatile and powerful solution for edge inference tasks. It combines high performance with energy efficiency and robust security, making it an ideal choice for our next-gen edge-AI product.

claims: Subject: Introducing NXP i.MX 95 for Our Next-Gen Edge-AI Product
I hope this email finds you well.
I wanted to share some exciting news about the NXP i.MX 95, which I believe will be a perfect fit for our new edge-AI product.
Let me give you a quick rundown on what it is, its Neutron NPU, and why it’s ideal for edge inference.
The NXP i.MX 95 is a powerful applications processor designed for advanced graphics, video, and machine learning acceleration.
It features a rich set of peripherals and processor cores that support these features, making it an excellent choice for energy-efficient edge computing.
6x Arm Cortex-A55 cores, up to 1.8 GHz.
1x Arm Cortex-M7 for real-time processing.
1x Arm Cortex-M33 for safety-critical tasks.
Supports up to 6400 MT/s in LPDDR5 mode.
High-speed interfaces like MIPI DSI, LVDS, and SPI.
Integrated EdgeLock secure enclave for enhanced security.
The NPU (Neuron Processing Unit) is a hardware accelerator that provides efficient processing of machine-learning workloads.
It supports up to 256 MACs/cycle, making it highly efficient for inference tasks.
Features like Weight Decoder, Rescaler/Shifter, and Activation Engine enable optimized neural network processing.
Efficiency**: The Neutron NPU is designed to handle the computational demands of neural networks efficiently, reducing the burden on the main CPU.
This not only improves performance but also conserves power, which is crucial for edge devices.
Customization**: The NPU supports a wide range of machine learning models, and its architecture allows for efficient memory management and data flow, which is essential for edge inference.
Scalability**: The i.MX 95 supports both low-power and high-performance inference, depending on the requirements of your application.
Whether you need fast inference times or lower power consumption, the i.MX 95 can handle it.
Security**: The integrated EdgeLock secure enclave ensures that sensitive data remains secure, which is a critical consideration for edge devices.
In summary, the NXP i.MX 95 with its Neutron NPU is a versatile and powerful solution for edge inference tasks.
It combines high performance with energy efficiency and robust security, making it an ideal choice for our next-gen edge-AI product.

The i.MX 95 Neutron NPU is a hardware accelerator designed to efficiently process machine-learning workloads. Here are its key features based on the provided excerpts:

- **Efficient Processing of Machine-Learning Workloads**: The NPU is integrated into the i.MX 95 processor to help deliver higher performance and lower power consumption for neural network (NN) inference tasks.

- **MAC Compute Blocks Throughput Management**: The NPU manages the throughput of Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) compute blocks, which are fundamental operations in neural network computations.

- **Optimization of Weights**: It optimizes the arrangement of weights to enhance the efficiency of neural network operations.

- **Memory Access Management**: The NPU efficiently manages memory accesses, which is crucial for the performance of neural network computations.

- **Activation Functions Support**: It supports a variety of activation functions, including ReLu, PreLu, and LeakyReLu, which are essential for determining the final value of a neuron in neural networks.

- **Rescaling and Pooling Functions**: The NPU supports

rows.prompt: Using the datasheets, what does the i.MX 95 Neutron NPU do, and what are its key features?
rows.raw:
The i.MX 95 Neutron NPU is a hardware accelerator designed to efficiently process machine learning workloads. Here are its key features based on the provided excerpts:

- **Efficient Processing**: The Neutron NPU is optimized to handle Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) operations, which are fundamental to neural network computations.
- **Weight Management**: It manages the arrangement of weights to optimize performance.
- **Memory Access Management**: The NPU handles memory accesses efficiently, which is crucial for reducing latency and improving throughput.
- **Activation Functions**: It supports various activation functions such as ReLu, PreLu, and LeakyReLu, which are necessary for determining the final value of a neuron in neural networks.
- **Sampling and Reshaping Functions**: These functions allow for flexible manipulation of data, which is important for neural network operations.
- **Element-wise Operations**: The NPU supports operations that apply to each element in an array independently.
- **Layer Operations**: It can perform operations related to different layers in a neural network, such as convolutional and fully connected layers

Memory Access Management**: The NPU handles memory accesses efficiently, which is crucial for reducing latency and improving throughput. Activation Functions**: It supports various activation functions such as ReLu, PreLu, and LeakyReLu, which are necessary for determining the final value of a neuron in neural networks. : **NXP i.MX 95 Product Brief**

---

**Overview:**
The NXP i.MX 95 is a high-performance, multi-core system-on-chip (SoC) designed for a wide range of applications, from industrial automation to smart home devices. It features a Cortex-A55 processor core with advanced machine learning (ML) capabilities, providing up to 2 TOP/s performance through the integrated NPU.

**NPU (Neural Processing Unit):**
The i.MX 95 includes an NPU that supports a variety of neural network operations, including convolutional neural networks (CNN), recurrent neural networks (RNN), and activation functions. The NPU is capable of 2.0 TOP/s performance with 1024 MACs operating at up to 1.0 GHz, making it well-suited for efficient ML workloads. It integrates seamlessly with the CPU, delivering high performance and lower power consumption for ML inference tasks.

**Memory and Connectivity:**
- **Memory:** The i.MX 95 supports LPDDR5/LPDDR4X memory with inline ECC and encryption, providing secure and high-speed memory access. It also includes 1492kB of OCRAM with ECC.
- **Connectivity:** The SoC features a range of high-speed interfaces, including 2x 1 GbE with TSN, 2x PCIe Gen 3.0 x12, 10 GbE with TSN, and 2x USB 3.0 + USB 2.0. Additional interfaces include MIPI-CSI, MIPI-DSI, 3x SD/SDIO3.0/eMMC5.1, and octal SPI flash with inline crypto.

**Target Markets:**
- **Industrial Automation:** With robust security features and high-performance connectivity, the i.MX 95 is ideal for industrial control systems, factory automation, and smart manufacturing applications.
- **Smart Home:** The integrated NPU and advanced connectivity make it suitable for smart home devices, such as security cameras, smart speakers, and home automation systems.
- **Consumer Electronics:** The i.MX 95 is well-suited for consumer electronics, including smart TVs, set-top boxes, and gaming consoles.
- **Automotive Infotainment:** The SoC's high-performance capabilities and security features make it a strong candidate for in-vehicle infotainment systems and ADAS (Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems).

---

PCI defines how such devices are discovered and integrated into the system. This includes: • Assignment of addresses for registers and memory in the device, determining how the "host system" accesses these • Assignment, configuration, and control of interrupts including various types of message signaled interrupts (MSI) • Reporting and handling certain errors • Handling power management including events that will cause the system to exit low power modes • Adding and removing such devices to a “live” system (hotplug) NXP Semiconductors Integrated Endpoint Root Complex (iEP-RC) i.MX 95 Applications Processor Reference Manual, Rev. 5, 2026-03-30 Reference Manual 6381 / 11263  PCI is defined for a multi-connect, parallel bus and PCIe for a serial interconnect. Devices can be arranged into a tree topology through the use of bridges or switches. Both PCI and PCIe are intended to be used with pluggable cards and are often used with peripherals on the same circuit board. None the less the use of PCI with peripheral devices which are integrated into an SoC is becoming common as it allows using the extensive standardized approaches and software infrastructure created for PCI with these integrated peripherals simplifying software development and portability across different SoCs. With PCI, system software (boot firmware, OS, …) is initially only aware of a PCI controller -- a device which acts as the bridge between the host and the PCI/PCIe. claims: : **NXP i.MX 95 Product Brief
The NXP i.MX 95 is a high-performance, multi-core system-on-chip (SoC) designed for a wide range of applications, from industrial automation to smart home devices.
It features a Cortex-A55 processor core with advanced machine learning (ML) capabilities, providing up to 2 TOP/s performance through the integrated NPU.
The i.MX 95 includes an NPU that supports a variety of neural network operations, including convolutional neural networks (CNN), recurrent neural networks (RNN), and activation functions.
The NPU is capable of 2.0 TOP/s performance with 1024 MACs operating at up to 1.0 GHz, making it well-suited for efficient ML workloads.
It integrates seamlessly with the CPU, delivering high performance and lower power consumption for ML inference tasks.
Memory:** The i.MX 95 supports LPDDR5/LPDDR4X memory with inline ECC and encryption, providing secure and high-speed memory access.
It also includes 1492kB of OCRAM with ECC.
Connectivity:** The SoC features a range of high-speed interfaces, including 2x 1 GbE with TSN, 2x PCIe Gen 3.0 x12, 10 GbE with TSN, and 2x USB 3.0 + USB 2.0.
Additional interfaces include MIPI-CSI, MIPI-DSI, 3x SD/SDIO3.0/eMMC5.1, and octal SPI flash with inline crypto.

Industrial Automation:** With robust security features and high-performance connectivity, the i.MX 95 is ideal for industrial control systems, factory automation, and smart manufacturing applications.
Smart Home:** The integrated NPU and advanced connectivity make it suitable for smart home devices, such as security cameras, smart speakers, and home automation systems.
Consumer Electronics:** The i.MX 95 is well-suited for consumer electronics, including smart TVs, set-top boxes, and gaming consoles.
Automotive Infotainment:** The SoC's high-performance capabilities and security features make it a strong candidate for in-vehicle infotainment systems and ADAS (Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems).

Certainly! Here's a concise one-page product brief for the NXP i.MX 95:

---

**NXP i.MX 95 Product Brief**

**Overview:**
The NXP i.MX 95 is a high-performance, versatile system-on-chip (SoC) designed for a wide range of industrial and embedded applications. It integrates multiple processing cores, high-speed memory, robust connectivity options, and advanced peripherals, making it suitable for complex and demanding environments. The i.MX 95 is available in various temperature grades, ensuring reliability in both industrial and automotive settings.

**NPU:**
The i.MX 95 features the Neutron N3-1024S NPU, an advanced hardware accelerator optimized for neural network (NN) inference. With a peak performance of 2.0 TOP/s, the NPU supports a variety of NN architectures including CNNs, RNNs, and activation functions. It also includes support for error detection and correction mechanisms, ensuring high reliability in mission-critical applications.

**Memory & Connectivity:**
- **Memory:** The i.MX 95 supports LPDDR5/LPDDR4X memory with inline ECC and encryption, offering high bandwidth and security. It also integrates 512kB TCM with ECC and 1492kB OCRAM (ECC) for efficient processing.
- **Connectivity:** The SoC supports high-speed interfaces such as two 1 GbE ports (with TSN), two PCIe Gen 3.0 x12, 10 GbE (with TSN), and multiple serial communication interfaces including USB 3.0, USB 2.0, CAN-FD, MIPI-CSI, MIPI-DSI, and more. These features enable seamless integration with various peripheral devices and networks.

**Target Markets:**
- **Industrial Automation:** The i.MX 95 is ideal for applications such as energy storage and management systems, smart meters, power line communications, and factory automation, where reliability and performance are critical.
- **Smart Home & IoT:** Suitable for smart speakers, home security and surveillance systems, and major home appliances, leveraging its energy efficiency and advanced connectivity options.
- **Mobile Robotics:** The SoC supports complex motion control and robotics applications, including BLDC and PMSM motor control, making it a robust choice for mobile robotics ecosystems.
- **Edge AI/ML:** With its NPU and high-performance processing capabilities, the i.MX 95 is well-suited for edge AI and machine learning applications, enabling real-time anomaly detection and predictive maintenance.

---

This brief provides a high-level overview of the i.MX 95's key features, focusing on the NPU, memory/connectivity, and target markets.

Block diagram 107.1.2 Features Below is a list of features supported on iEP-RC: • Presents as a PCIe Root Complex that contains Event Collectors, and integrates with Integrated End Point (RCiEP or iEP) - For easy software discovery of peripheral functions and error reporting; leverage the infrastructure built into OSes and RTOS for PCIe. • Discoverable capabilities at a granular level - Software can discover what features/capabilities exists; allow an easy upgrade path. • 7'd2 ECAM buses to provide access to the PCIe Config space of the iEP and RCEC • 7'd2 Root Complex Event Collectors (RCEC) • Generate PCIe wired interrupt to the system on receiving error or Power Management Event message from iEP 107.1.3 PCI/PCIe Background It is useful to have an understanding of PCI/PCIe to be able to understand PCI Root Complex Integrated Endpoints. This section is intended to give an overview for those not familiar with PCI, not to provide a detailed explanation. 107.1.3.1 Overview PCI and its successor PCI Express (PCIe) provide a framework for connecting peripheral devices to a computer consisting of one or more CPU(s) and memory. PCI defines how such devices are discovered and integrated into the system. This includes: • Assignment of addresses for registers and memory in the device, determining how the "host system" accesses these • Assignment, configuration, and control of interrupts including various types of message signaled interrupts (MSI) • Reporting and handling certain errors • Handling power management including events that will cause the system to exit low power modes • Adding and removing such devices to a “live” system (hotplug) NXP Semiconductors Integrated Endpoint Root Complex (iEP-RC) i.MX 95 Applications Processor Reference Manual, Rev. 5, 2026-03-30 Reference Manual 6381 / 11263  PCI is defined for a multi-connect, parallel bus and PCIe for a serial interconnect. Devices can be arranged into a tree topology through the use of bridges or switches. Both PCI and PCIe are intended to be used with pluggable cards and are often used with peripherals on the same circuit board. None the less the use of PCI with peripheral devices which are integrated into an SoC is becoming common as it allows using the extensive standardized approaches and software infrastructure created for PCI with these integrated peripherals simplifying software development and portability across different SoCs. With PCI, system software (boot firmware, OS, …) is initially only aware of a PCI controller -- a device which acts as the bridge between the host and the PCI/PCIe. It is not aware of any devices connected to this controller.

claims: The NXP i.MX 95 is a high-performance, versatile system-on-chip (SoC) designed for a wide range of industrial and embedded applications.
It integrates multiple processing cores, high-speed memory, robust connectivity options, and advanced peripherals, making it suitable for complex and demanding environments.
The i.MX 95 is available in various temperature grades, ensuring reliability in both industrial and automotive settings.
The i.MX 95 features the Neutron N3-1024S NPU, an advanced hardware accelerator optimized for neural network (NN) inference.
With a peak performance of 2.0 TOP/s, the NPU supports a variety of NN architectures including CNNs, RNNs, and activation functions.
It also includes support for error detection and correction mechanisms, ensuring high reliability in mission-critical applications.
Memory:** The i.MX 95 supports LPDDR5/LPDDR4X memory with inline ECC and encryption, offering high bandwidth and security.
It also integrates 512kB TCM with ECC and 1492kB OCRAM (ECC) for efficient processing.

Connectivity:** The SoC supports high-speed interfaces such as two 1 GbE ports (with TSN), two PCIe Gen 3.0 x12, 10 GbE (with TSN), and multiple serial communication interfaces including USB 3.0, USB 2.0, CAN-FD, MIPI-CSI, MIPI-DSI, and more.
These features enable seamless integration with various peripheral devices and networks.

Industrial Automation:** The i.MX 95 is ideal for applications such as energy storage and management systems, smart meters, power line communications, and factory automation, where reliability and performance are critical.
Smart Home & IoT:** Suitable for smart speakers, home security and surveillance systems, and major home appliances, leveraging its energy efficiency and advanced connectivity options.
Mobile Robotics:** The SoC supports complex motion control and robotics applications, including BLDC and PMSM motor control, making it a robust choice for mobile robotics ecosystems.

Edge AI/ML:** With its NPU and high-performance processing capabilities, the i.MX 95 is well-suited for edge AI and machine learning applications, enabling real-time anomaly detection and predictive maintenance.
This brief provides a high-level overview of the i.MX 95's key features, focusing on the NPU, memory/connectivity, and target markets.

:

**NXP i.MX 95 Product Brief**

---

**Overview:**
The NXP i.MX 95 is a high-performance, multi-core application processor designed for industrial and automotive applications. It features a 64-bit Arm Cortex-A55 and Cortex-M33 cores, supporting up to 512 KB of TCM and 1492 KB of OCRAM with ECC, ensuring robust performance and reliability. The processor supports a wide range of communication protocols including CAN-FD, I3C, I2C, SPI, and UART, along with high-speed interfaces such as 2x 1 GbE, 2x PCIe Gen 3.0, 10 GbE (w/TSN), and multiple MIPI interfaces (CSI, DSI).

**NPU:**
The i.MX 95 integrates the eIQ Neutron N3-1024S NPU, a hardware accelerator for machine learning (ML) workloads. This NPU supports up to 2 TOP/s performance with 1024 MACs operating at 1.0 GHz. It natively supports convolutional neural networks (CNN), recurrent neural networks (RNN), and various activation functions, making it ideal for edge AI applications. The NPU can handle up to 2 OPS/MAC and offers efficient processing of ML workloads, optimizing weights, managing memory accesses, and providing rescaling, activation, and pooling functions.

**Memory/Connectivity:**
- **Memory:** The i.MX 95 supports LPDDR5/LPDDR4X memory with inline ECC and encryption, up to 2 MB of Flash memory, and 512 KB of TCM (ECC) and 1492 KB of OCRAM (ECC). It also supports XSPI responders for high-speed memory interfaces.
- **Connectivity:** The processor includes 2x 1 GbE, 2x PCIe Gen 3.0, 10 GbE (w/TSN), 2x CAN-FD, 3x SD/SDIO3.0, and eMMC5.1. It also supports 8-channel 12-bit ADC, 2-lane I2S TDM, and 4-lane LVDS interfaces, making it suitable for various industrial and automotive applications.

**Target Markets:**
- **Industrial Applications:** Energy storage and management systems, smart meters, power line communication, factory automation, and industrial HMI.
- **Automotive Applications:** ADAS systems, infotainment, and connected vehicle solutions.
- **Consumer Applications:** Smart home devices, smart speakers, soundbars, and gaming accessories.

---

This brief covers the essential features of the i.MX 95, highlighting its NPU capabilities, memory and connectivity features, and the target markets where it excels.

This section is intended to give an overview for those not familiar with PCI, not to provide a detailed explanation. 107.1.3.1 Overview PCI and its successor PCI Express (PCIe) provide a framework for connecting peripheral devices to a computer consisting of one or more CPU(s) and memory. PCI defines how such devices are discovered and integrated into the system. This includes: • Assignment of addresses for registers and memory in the device, determining how the "host system" accesses these • Assignment, configuration, and control of interrupts including various types of message signaled interrupts (MSI) • Reporting and handling certain errors • Handling power management including events that will cause the system to exit low power modes • Adding and removing such devices to a “live” system (hotplug) NXP Semiconductors Integrated Endpoint Root Complex (iEP-RC) i.MX 95 Applications Processor Reference Manual, Rev. 5, 2026-03-30 Reference Manual 6381 / 11263  PCI is defined for a multi-connect, parallel bus and PCIe for a serial interconnect. Devices can be arranged into a tree topology through the use of bridges or switches. Both PCI and PCIe are intended to be used with pluggable cards and are often used with peripherals on the same circuit board. None the less the use of PCI with peripheral devices which are integrated into an SoC is becoming common as it allows using the extensive standardized approaches and software infrastructure created for PCI with these integrated peripherals simplifying software development and portability across different SoCs. With PCI, system software (boot firmware, OS, …) is initially only aware of a PCI controller -- a device which acts as the bridge between the host and the PCI/PCIe. It is not aware of any devices connected to this controller.

claims: The NXP i.MX 95 is a high-performance, multi-core application processor designed for industrial and automotive applications.
It features a 64-bit Arm Cortex-A55 and Cortex-M33 cores, supporting up to 512 KB of TCM and 1492 KB of OCRAM with ECC, ensuring robust performance and reliability.

The processor supports a wide range of communication protocols including CAN-FD, I3C, I2C, SPI, and UART, along with high-speed interfaces such as 2x 1 GbE, 2x PCIe Gen 3.0, 10 GbE (w/TSN), and multiple MIPI interfaces (CSI, DSI).
The i.MX 95 integrates the eIQ Neutron N3-1024S NPU, a hardware accelerator for machine learning (ML) workloads.
This NPU supports up to 2 TOP/s performance with 1024 MACs operating at 1.0 GHz.
It natively supports convolutional neural networks (CNN), recurrent neural networks (RNN), and various activation functions, making it ideal for edge AI applications.
The NPU can handle up to 2 OPS/MAC and offers efficient processing of ML workloads, optimizing weights, managing memory accesses, and providing rescaling, activation, and pooling functions.
Memory:** The i.MX 95 supports LPDDR5/LPDDR4X memory with inline ECC and encryption, up to 2 MB of Flash memory, and 512 KB of TCM (ECC) and 1492 KB of OCRAM (ECC).
It also supports XSPI responders for high-speed memory interfaces.
Connectivity:** The processor includes 2x 1 GbE, 2x PCIe Gen 3.0, 10 GbE (w/TSN), 2x CAN-FD, 3x SD/SDIO3.0, and eMMC5.1.
It also supports 8-channel 12-bit ADC, 2-lane I2S TDM, and 4-lane LVDS interfaces, making it suitable for various industrial and automotive applications.
Industrial Applications:** Energy storage and management systems, smart meters, power line communication, factory automation, and industrial HMI.
Automotive Applications:** ADAS systems, infotainment, and connected vehicle solutions.
Consumer Applications:** Smart home devices, smart speakers, soundbars, and gaming accessories.
This brief covers the essential features of the i.MX 95, highlighting its NPU capabilities, memory and connectivity features, and the target markets where it excels.
